name: Question 2
problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y+3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}{x},\,y(1)=1,\,x>0.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation*

$$
\frac{dz}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}z=-3x
$$

*using the substitution $z={y}^{-1}.$*
worked_solution:
The substitution $z={y}^{-1}$ transforms the given equation into the equation

$$
\frac{dz}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}z=-3x.
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)\,.
$$

with

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x)=\frac{1}{x},\,Q(x)=-3x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\int (1/x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\  & =x\end{aligned}
$$

under the condition that $x>0.$

Multiplying both sides of the standard form equation by $I(x)=x$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (\frac{dz}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}z) & =x\cdot (-3x) \\ x\cdot \frac{dz}{dx}+z & =-3{x}^{2} \\ \frac{d}{dx}(xz) & =-3{x}^{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{d}{dx}(xz)\,dx & =-\int 3{x}^{2}\,dx \\ xz & =-{x}^{3}+C \\ z & =\frac{C-{x}^{3}}{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine $y(x)$ by writing $z={y}^{-1}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{-1} & =\frac{C-{x}^{3}}{x} \\ y & =\frac{x}{C-{x}^{3}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We now determine $C$ from the initial condition $y(1)=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{1}{C-1}\,⟹\,C=2\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{x}{2-{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Solve the initial value problem dydx=y+3x2y2x,y(1)=1,x>0. Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation dzdx+1xz=−3x using the substitution z=y−1.

a
y=2x1+x3
b
y=2x1+x
c
y=x2/3
d
y=−2x1−3x3
e
y=x2−x3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The substitution z=y−1 transforms the given equation into the equation dzdx+1xz=−3x.

The above equation is in the standard form dzdx+P(x)z=Q(x). with P(x)=1x,Q(x)=−3x.

We then compute an integrating factor: I(x)=e∫P(x)dx=e∫(1/x)dx=eln⁡x=x

under the condition that x>0.

Multiplying both sides of the standard form equation by I(x)=x yields x⋅(dzdx+1xz)=x⋅(−3x)x⋅dzdx+z=−3x2ddx(xz)=−3x2.

So, we have ∫ddx(xz)dx=−∫3x2dxxz=−x3+Cz=C−x3x.

Next, we determine y(x) by writing z=y−1. This results in y−1=C−x3xy=xC−x3.

We now determine C from the initial condition y(1)=1: 1=1C−1⟹C=2

So we have y=x2−x3.
